newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hungary may have overcharged U.S. for Bosnia buses.
newsitem.headline: Hungary may have overcharged U.S. for Bosnia buses.

text.p: The Hungarian government may have overcharged the U.S. army by more than $1 million in passenger bus contracts for the NATO-led Bosnia peace mission, the newspaper Stars and Stripes reported on Thursday.

The newspaper, which serves the U.S. military community in Europe and Asia, said a draft report by the army's headquarters in Europe found "significant price variances" in a review of $2.6 million worth of written and verbal bus contracts.
However, officials at the army's European command headquarters in Heidelberg said the internal audit obtained by the Stars and Stripes was only preliminary and was flawed.

"This is a preliminary report that we think is very flawed," an army spokeswoman told Reuters. "We are now doing an aggressive investigation into this matter. The support from the Hungarians during this mission has been tremendous."
The army report, dated September 11, said that, based on independent price quotes obtained, about $1.2 million of $1.9 million paid for buses up to August 7 were overcharges.
Rates varied from $1.12 per mile to $7.61 per mile for buses carrying soldiers from bases in Hungary to Croatia and Bosnia.
In one instance, the newspaper said two bus companies competing for the same contract submitted identical bids and both were higher than the previously contracted service. Both companies were hired.
Rates charged to the army exceeded independent quotes by between 209 percent and 368 percent, the newspaper said.

Auditors also found apparent overcharging in rail transport prices and have recommended a review of all of the army's $32 million worth of contracts with the Hungarian ministry of defence, the newspaper said.
